sites.n: Kharyaga-Usinsk pipeline leaks (Komi oil spill)
sites.cs: List-only: no official coordinate.
sites.kf: World Bank: leaks from the Kharyaga-Usinsk pipeline caused one of the world's largest oil spills; in autumn 1994 over 20,000 tons (140,000 barrels) entered the Kolva River when temporary dikes failed in heavy rains.
sites.vol: in excess of 100,000 tons (730,000 barrels) trapped in bogs and creeks; over 20,000 tons to the Kolva River (World Bank)

sites.n: Greenpoint oil spill (former refineries and terminals), Newtown Creek, Brooklyn
sites.cs: EPA FRS registry ID 110001570700 ('EXXONMOBIL GREENPOINT REMEDIATION PROJECT, 300 N Henry St, Brooklyn') Latitude83/Longitude83
sites.kf: NYSDEC: a Coast Guard patrol saw oil entering Newtown Creek at Meeker Avenue on 2 Sept 1978; the spill area exceeded 52 acres and was estimated in 1979 at about 17 million gallons. NY Attorney General: the 2010 settlement (State of New York v. ExxonMobil, E.D.N.Y. 07-CV-2902) requires full cleanup and about $25 million in payments.

sites.st: Active remediation under the 2010 federal consent decree

sites.n: Red Hill Bulk Fuel Storage Facility (Navy), Oahu
sites.cs: EPA FRS registry ID 110019898869 ('HALAWA RED HILL (Red Hill fuel tank farms)') Latitude83/Longitude83
sites.kf: EPA: a May 2021 pressure surge released over 19,000 gallons of JP-5 that sat in a fire-suppression drain line until it ruptured on 20 Nov 2021, contaminating the Red Hill well; about 93,000 Navy water-system users were affected. DLNR: about 14,000 gallons of fuel is believed to have entered the Red Hill Shaft system.
sites.vol: over 19,000 gallons released 6 May 2021 (EPA); up to 19,377 gallons spilled 20 Nov 2021, up to 5,542 unrecovered (Navy)

sites.ty: JP-5 jet fuel in the Red Hill Shaft drinking-water source and groundwater
sites.st: Closure and groundwater cleanup under the 2023 Consent Order
sites.dt: WWII-era tanks; 2021 releases; defueling and closure

sites.n: Kirtland AFB Bulk Fuels Facility jet-fuel plume, Albuquerque
sites.cs: EPA FRS registry ID 110015742758 ('KIRTLAND AIR FORCE BASE (installation-level)') Latitude83/Longitude83
sites.kf: USAF (2011): between 1950 and 1999 a 16-inch underground offloading pipe leaked; pressure tests in Nov 1999 revealed the discharge; fuel reached groundwater about 500 ft down and migrated off base toward Albuquerque drinking-water wells. NMED oversees corrective action (2026 monitoring reports posted).
sites.vol: 2 to 8 million gallons (USAF, 2011); reported later estimates up to 24 million gallons (ATSDR range 3 to 24 million; document could not be opened at this check)

sites.ty: Aviation gasoline, JP-4 and JP-8; ethylene dibromide (EDB) in the regional aquifer

sites.n: Former Texaco/Petroecuador consortium oil fields (Lago Agrio litigation area), Oriente
sites.cs: List-only: no official coordinate.
sites.kf: A Permanent Court of Arbitration tribunal (Case 2009-23) issued its Second Partial Award on 30 Aug 2018. Reported: the award ruled for Chevron and Texaco against Ecuador, and a 2014 U.S. federal court opinion (Chevron v. Donziger, S.D.N.Y.) held that the 2011 Lago Agrio judgment against Chevron was obtained by fraud and bribery. Neither text was read in full here.

sites.n: Ogoniland oil contamination (UNEP assessment)
sites.cs: List-only: no official point read (UNEP site fact sheets not checked for coordinates).
